learning: Iteration 9 (0.14 m track) scored 69.05, below iteration 6, with line losses unchanged at 1.0 per run on the s-bend and slalom. Turn rate is therefore not the limit at this gain. The remaining untested single lever is wheel_radius (0.035 m), which the Builder has flagged for the final iteration.
notes: Iteration 10 package: the iteration 6 best design (70.83) restored exactly, with wheel_track 0.12 m as the Builder proposed. The controller is unchanged, so this race is a clean confirmation of the base.
rationale: The Builder's iteration 10 proposal restores the iteration 6 geometry (70.83, the best result). The only change from iteration 9 is wheel_track back to 0.12 m. Iteration 9 (0.14 m track, 69.05) showed that a wider track neither removed the s-bend and slalom line losses nor raised the score, so turn rate is not the limit. Every geometry lever tested at 12 mm footprints has either lowered the score or left line losses at 1.0 per run: mass 0.4 kg is at its floor, body_length 0.12 m lowered the score, y 0.07 m did not help, 8 mm footprints lowered it, the ±0.04 m span collapsed the s-bend (36.6), and the 0.14 m track lowered it. I therefore accept the geometry exactly as proposed. The controller is kept identical to iteration 6 (kp 3.0, ki 0, kd 0.2, base_speed 1.5, last_direction recovery, weights +1, +0.5, 0, -0.5, -1). Any controller change now would confound this confirmation race, and the only gain change tried (iteration 1) was confounded with a narrower track and scored lower. Expected result, as a prediction only: a score near 70.8 with about 1.0 line-loss event per run on the s-bend and slalom. Any difference would come from seed or track noise, since the design is unchanged from iteration 6.
